messages:
maria: Heads up — started the canary for model phi-v2 (canary id: phi-v2-2026-03) scoped to eu region. Noticing routing fallback is spilling traffic from enterprise tier to standard tier model variants. Need guidance on per-tier rollout scoping + fallback behavior.

sam: thanks. can you paste the routing policy you used?

maria: sure — current simple policy (yaml) we pushed via /routing/update: 

```
routing_policy:
  - match: {region: 'eu-1'}
    preferred: ["phi-v2-2026-03"]
    fallback: ["phi-v1-stable","phi-v1-quant"]
```

maria: that works but because our smart-router also has global tier-aware fallback rules, when phi-v2 becomes unhealthy it routes to the nearest compatible variant which includes lower-tier quantized versions. enterprise traffic started getting served by standard-tier quantized variants — customer noticed.

noah: hmm — expected behavior is: per-tier scoping on rollouts should prevent downgrade across tiers. We should support an explicit `rollout_scope` in the routing API so the router knows to only consider fallbacks within the same tier unless explicit cross-tier fallback is allowed.

jia: Agreed. Proposal: extend the routing payload with an optional `rollout_scope` block. Example: 

```
rollout_scope:
  tiers: ["enterprise"]
  regions: ["eu-1"]
  allow_cross_tier_fallback: false
```

sam: API-wise that could be additive. Router can evaluate fallback candidates in two passes: first match same-tier candidates, then if `allow_cross_tier_fallback` true fall back to others. Otherwise failover to configured route-level fallback.

oliver: important telemetry hooks: we need per-tier fallback counters and per-rollout fallback rates surfaced in the Console. Right now Console aggregates fallbacks by model id but not by tier. Customers care if enterprise traffic dropped to standard quantized models.

maria: +1. Also need an alert rule: if cross-tier fallback ratio > X% within Y minutes for a canary scoped to a tier, escalate.

noah: UX idea for Console: rollout modal should show scoping checkboxes (tiers, regions) and a toggle: "Allow cross-tier fallback (unsafe)" with a tooltip explaining cost/SL impacts. Also show an estimated fallback impact preview based on traffic profiles.

sam: engineering caveat: our existing smart-router picks candidates using capacity and latency budgets. If we restrict to tier-only candidates there may be no available capacity and requests will queue or error. Need to define behavior: queue, fail-fast, or route to fallback in other tier. Which do we prefer?

jia: default should be to failover according to the rollout_scope policy. e.g. if `allow_cross_tier_fallback=false` and no same-tier candidate found, then return 503 + metric tag `no_same_tier_candidate`. But Console can offer an opt-in policy for automatic cross-tier fallback with soft throttling.

oliver: for on-call ops, prefer fail-fast + clear observability. We can create an automated remediation in the rollout controller to temporarily expand scope if error budget triggers. But that must be explicit and auditable.

maria: sample router decision pseudocode I sketched: 

```
candidates = find_candidates(request)
if rollout_scope.tiers:
  same_tier = filter(candidates, tier in rollout_scope.tiers)
  if same_tier.non_empty:
    select_best(same_tier)
  else if rollout_scope.allow_cross_tier_fallback:
    select_best(candidates)
  else:
    return 503, metric=\"no_same_tier_candidate\"
else:
  select_best(candidates)
```

sam: looks reasonable. Implementation note: `find_candidates` must be cheap — avoid full model metadata lookups in the hot path. Cache tier attributes on the routing table and invalidate on policy changes.

noah: product ask: Console should show a per-rollout "fallback map" that previews where traffic will go if each candidate fails (tier-preserving and cross-tier). This helps selling canary safety to enterprise customers.

maria: + mention: need to update rollout docs and the SDKs. SDK currently only supports `preferred_models` and `fallback_models` arrays. Add `rollout_scope` and a `scope_enforcement` enum ["fail_fast","expand_scope"] to let customers choose behavior.

sam: internal API debate: instead of adding new fields to routing API, we could reuse existing `policy_tags` on models and let the router evaluate tag expressions like `tier:enterprise AND region:eu-1`. Pros: no API churn and flexible. Cons: harder UX and error-prone for users.

jia: Tags are flexible but opaque for non-engineers. For Console and clear SLAs, explicit `rollout_scope` is better. Keep tag-based matching as advanced mode.

oliver: telemetry details: track `fallback_attempts`, `fallback_successes`, `no_same_tier_candidate`, `cross_tier_fallbackes` (typo: cross_tier_fallbacks) with labels [model_from, model_to, tier_from, tier_to, region]. Those labels help debug impact and cost differences.

release-bot: [release-bot] Canary phi-v2-2026-03 started at 2026-03-18T10:02:47Z, scope: regions=[eu-1], tiers=[enterprise], id=phi-v2-2026-03

maria: seeing initial telemetry: fallback rate 2.7% in first 5m, 95% of those are to phi-v1-quant (standard tier). Posting graphs in #eng-observability. :eyes:

noah: ok action items: 
- sam/jia: design router change to honor `rollout_scope` and implement candidate pass logic.
- sam/oliver: add metrics/tags and ensure router emits `no_same_tier_candidate`.
- product (noah): update Console mockups to include scope controls + fallback preview.
- docs: SDK + routing API docs for `rollout_scope` and `scope_enforcement`.

maria: I'll pause the canary if fallback rate exceeds 5% for 10m. keeping us posted.

sam: will sketch a PR for the router changes and share an RFC by EOD.

oliver: I'll add a Grafana panel template for per-rollout fallback heatmaps.

maria: thanks all.
